name: Naval Ravikant
milestone_by_age_26: In 1999 at age 24–25 he co-founded Epinions, a consumer product-review site that raised ~$45M in venture capital from Benchmark and August Capital.
early_history_summary: Born New Delhi 1974; immigrated to NYC at 9 with mother and brother after parents separated; raised modestly in Queens. Attended Stuyvesant High School (grad 1991) and Dartmouth (CS + economics, 1995). Brief BCG stint, then Silicon Valley; Epinions (1999) was the breakout founding.
primary_leverage_engine: Technical depth + product execution in early consumer web
family_context_summary: Father was a pharmacist in India; after immigration credentials did not transfer and parents separated; mother raised Naval and brother Kamal in Queens with long hours and night school; modest/immigrant single-parent household.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father pharmacist (India); not a tech-domain apprenticeship path. Mother clerical work / night school; no documented tech industry transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stuyvesant, Dartmouth CS, immigrant single-parent, Epinions founding, self-sufficiency
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Dartmouth Alumni Magazine agree birth Nov 5 1974, Stuyvesant/Dartmouth path, and Epinions cofounding in 1999 (~age 24–25) with major VC. Later AngelList (2010) is post-26. Family is documented as modest immigrant single-parent; adversity catalyst is clear; elite schools provided pipeline without family tech wealth.
starting_point: Born New Delhi 1974 to a pharmacist father; immigrated to Queens at 9 and raised by a working single mother after parents separated.
current_position: Cofounder/chairman of AngelList; angel investor (Uber, Twitter, etc.), author/podcast figure (Almanack of Naval); Forbes Self-Made 250 mention in 2026.

trajectory.event: Graduated Dartmouth with degrees in computer science and economics.
Co-founded Epinions, a product-review site that raised roughly $45M from top-tier VCs.
Epinions/Shopping.com IPO path completed after merger with Dealtime; later sued over founder equity treatment.
Started Venture Hacks blog and Hit Forge angel fund; early investments including Twitter/Uber.
Co-founded AngelList as a platform connecting startups and angel investors.
AngelList Venture raised capital at a reported ~$4B valuation.

name: Liang Rubo
milestone_by_age_26: In 2009 at about age 26 he co-founded the vertical real-estate search portal Jiujiufang (99fang) with college roommate Zhang Yiming—a material startup founding before ByteDance.
early_history_summary: Born 1983 in Jiangxi Yichun; met Zhang Yiming at Nankai University (microelectronics, graduated 2005). After early jobs the pair cofounded Jiujiufang in 2009; in 2012 they cofounded ByteDance, where Liang led product R&D on Toutiao and later Douyin/Lark before becoming CEO in 2021.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond birthplace Jiangxi Yichun and Nankai education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Nankai roommate Zhang Yiming, Jiujiufang cofounding, ByteDance product lead, microelectronics training
evidence_summary: Caixin and Baidu Baike both place birth in 1983, Nankai graduation 2005, and cofounding of Jiujiufang with Zhang in 2009 (~age 25–26). ByteDance cofounding in 2012 is post-26 (~29). Long-running Zhang partnership is the dominant documented advantage; family wealth/domain not documented.
starting_point: Born 1983 in Jiangxi Yichun, China; family class/occupations not documented in reviewed sources; Nankai University microelectronics path.
current_position: Chairman/CEO of ByteDance (TikTok parent); Forbes-listed self-made billionaire (~age 43 as of 2026 lists); based in Beijing.

trajectory.event: Graduated Nankai University in microelectronics; long-term partnership with roommate Zhang Yiming begins.
Co-founded real-estate portal Jiujiufang (99fang) with Zhang Yiming.
Co-founded ByteDance; led product R&D on Toutiao and early core systems.
Led Lark/Feishu cloud office product unit at ByteDance.
Succeeded Zhang Yiming as ByteDance CEO amid regulatory and global expansion pressure.

name: Balaji Srinivasan
milestone_by_age_26: No material dated career milestone by age 26 found; he completed Stanford BS/MS/PhD work through ~2006 (age 26) and taught briefly, but breakout cofounding of Counsyl was 2007–2008 at age ~27–28.
early_history_summary: Born May 24 1980 on Long Island to physician parents from Tamil Nadu; Stanford EE BS/MS/PhD plus chemical engineering MS; taught stats/bioinformatics then cofounded Counsyl (~2008), later a16z GP, Earn.com/Coinbase CTO, Network State author.
family_context_summary: Son of physician parents who immigrated from Tamil Nadu, India; raised in Plainview, Long Island.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents physicians; medical-family background, not documented as software/crypto apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Balaji anthology timeline place birth 1980 and Stanford degrees through ~2006; Counsyl cofounding ~2008 (age 27–28) is the first clear material startup milestone—after 26. PhD completion alone is treated as education, not the career breakout.

name: Daniel Mack
milestone_by_age_26: No reliable birth year or specific dated material milestone by age 26 found; known mainly as a systemd/Linux contributor (with Poettering et al.) without a publicly dated early career breakout tied to age.
early_history_summary: Appears in systemd contributor/NEWS lists and as part of the broader systemd core circle; no full biographical profile with birth year or early dated awards/foundings in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Public systemd/Linux mailing-list and project credits confirm contribution; no Wikipedia biography with birth year or a dated ≤26 milestone verifiable to two sources.

name: Emma Brunskill
category: Computer scientist, reinforcement learning / AI for education
milestone_by_age_26: Around 2000–2001 (~age 19–20) she won a Rhodes Scholarship after entering the University of Washington at 15 and graduating magna cum laude in computer engineering and physics in 2000; she earned an Oxford neuroscience master's in 2002.
early_history_summary: Grew up Seattle/Edmonds; early-entry UW at 15; Goldwater/Mary Gates/Anderson scholar; Rhodes to Magdalen College Oxford (neuroscience MSc 2002); MIT PhD 2009 (Nicholas Roy); NSF postdoc Berkeley; CMU faculty 2011 then Stanford associate professor from 2017; AAAI Fellow 2025.
primary_leverage_engine: Early intellectual specialization + elite academic pipeline
family_context_summary: Grew up in Seattle and Edmonds, Washington; detailed parental occupations/wealth not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: college at 15, Rhodes Scholar, Goldwater, MIT PhD, Stanford faculty
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and UW Magazine document early UW entry at 15, 2000 graduation, and Rhodes Scholarship (UW Rhodes cohort around 2000–2001), all well before age 26. Birth year ~1980 inferred from age-15 entry and 2000 graduation; Rhodes is a dated material milestone with two independent sources.
starting_point: Grew up in Seattle/Edmonds, Washington; entered University of Washington as an early-entry student at age 15; family occupations not documented.
current_position: Associate professor of computer science at Stanford University (courtesy GSE); AAAI Fellow (2025); research in reinforcement learning and AI for education/healthcare.

trajectory.event: Graduated UW magna cum laude in computer engineering and physics; selected as a Rhodes Scholar.
Completed Oxford master's in neuroscience at Magdalen College; summer work in Rwanda on school computing.
Earned MIT PhD in computer science on sequential decision making under Nicholas Roy.
Joined Carnegie Mellon as assistant professor of computer science after Berkeley NSF postdoc.
Received NSF CAREER Award; later ONR Young Investigator (2015).
Moved to Stanford University as computer science faculty.
Elected AAAI Fellow for RL and AI-for-education contributions.

name: Murray Campbell
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year; BSc Alberta 1979, MSc 1981, PhD CMU 1987; major public milestones (HiTech/ChipTest mid-1980s, Deep Thought, Deep Blue 1996–97) appear to fall after typical mid-20s, and age ≤26 cannot be verified.
early_history_summary: Canadian CS path via University of Alberta then Carnegie Mellon computer-chess research (HiTech, ChipTest, Deep Thought); joined IBM 1989 on Deep Blue; shared Fredkin Prize 1997 after Kasparov match.
evidence_summary: IBM Research profile and Wikipedia document degrees and Deep Blue role; without a verified birth year, age at mid-1980s chess-machine work cannot be shown ≤26 to the required standard.

name: William Hockey
milestone_by_age_26: At age 21 (~2010–2012) he cofounded Plaid with Zachary Perret in New York, building bank-linking infrastructure later used by major fintech apps.
early_history_summary: Born Sept 21 1989 in San Luis Obispo; rural California family-of-builders upbringing; Emory (CS/economics/history/finance); Bain internship met Perret; cofounded Plaid at 21, raised seed and scaled in SF; left day-to-day ~2019; launched Column bank 2022.
family_context_summary: Grew up rural/central California among farmers, welders, and craftspeople; described as a family of builders; not documented as tech wealth.
parent_family_domain_summary: Hands-on builder/practical-maker family culture; not a finance/tech industry family transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Perret cofounder, Emory+Bain, fintech API wave, rural builder mindset, Plaid at 21
evidence_summary: Wikipedia states birth Sept 21 1989 and founding Plaid at 21; Forbes/Emory profiles corroborate Plaid cofounding and later Column. Cofounder Perret and fintech-infrastructure wave are primary documented levers; family is rural builders not inherited capital.
starting_point: Born 1989 in San Luis Obispo, California; raised in rural central California in a hands-on 'family of builders' milieu.
current_position: Cofounder/CEO of Column (fintech infrastructure bank); Plaid board director; Scale AI board; previously Plaid cofounder/CTO/president.

trajectory.event: Met cofounder Zach Perret at Bain internship; began path to founding Plaid.
Cofounded Plaid and moved into bank-linking infrastructure after early consumer-finance experiments.
Stepped down from day-to-day Plaid role after multi-billion valuation trajectory.
Visa agreed to buy Plaid for $5.3B (deal later blocked by DOJ); founders became fintech royalty.
Plaid Series D at reported ~$13.4B valuation after Visa deal collapse.
Launched Column, a nationally chartered bank for fintech developers.

name: Arquay Harris
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found; documented career (CNET/CBS → Google → Slack 2016 senior eng leadership → Webflow VP Eng 2021; Forbes Top 50 Women in Tech 2018) cannot be dated to age ≤26.
early_history_summary: James Madison University BA; Academy of Art fine arts; technical production at CNET then software at CBS; Google web development manager; Slack senior director of engineering; Webflow VP of engineering from 2021.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Forbes profile confirm senior roles and 2018 Women in Tech recognition but give no birth year or dated ≤26 material milestone.

name: Kevin Hale
milestone_by_age_26: Wufoo was cofounded and entered YC W06 in 2006—a material founding—but independent birth-year confirmation beyond the curated candidate list (1980) was not found in reviewed sources, so age ≤26 cannot be verified to the two-source standard.
early_history_summary: Cofounded Wufoo (online form builder) with Chris and Ryan Campbell; YC Winter 2006; SurveyMonkey later acquired Wufoo; became YC partner teaching product/user-love frameworks.
evidence_summary: YC company page and Hale talks confirm Wufoo founding/YC W06 2006; birth year not independently corroborated in Wikipedia or major profiles reviewed, so eligibility fails the dated age≤26 bar.

name: Searge (Michael Stoyke)
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found; known for founding Mod Coder Pack (MCP) and joining Mojang as Minecraft developer (announced late 2013, started Jan 2014)—age at those events cannot be verified ≤26.
early_history_summary: Michael 'Searge' Stoyke founded MCP for Minecraft reverse-engineering/modding; hired by Mojang Studios; later Minecraft Java tech lead (gameplay).
evidence_summary: Minecraft Wiki documents MCP founding and Mojang hire; no birth year or age-dated early milestone in reviewed sources.

name: Meg Whitman
milestone_by_age_26: No material career breakout by age 26; Princeton AB 1977 and Harvard MBA 1979 led to early P&G brand-manager work (~age 23), but fame and material success arrived much later (eBay CEO from 1998 at age 41).
early_history_summary: Born Aug 4 1956 Cold Spring Harbor NY into a well-connected family; Princeton economics 1977; HBS MBA 1979; P&G, Bain, Disney, Stride Rite, FTD, Hasbro/Playskool; eBay CEO 1998–2008; HP/HPE CEO; Quibi; US Ambassador to Kenya 2022–2024.
family_context_summary: Daughter of Margaret Cushing Goodhue and Hendricks Hallett Whitman Jr.; lineage includes political and professional notables; affluent Long Island upbringing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Established professional/political family lineage; not primarily a tech-domain apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia documents elite education and early corporate jobs but the defining eBay CEO milestone is 1998 (age 41). Entry-level/junior corporate roles by 26 are not treated as material success milestones under the rubric.

name: Brian Grant
milestone_by_age_26: No birth year found; Kubernetes (2014) and Google Borg/Omega work are mid-career; LinkedIn notes 30+ years experience and a CS PhD, but no dated material milestone verifiably at age ≤26.
early_history_summary: CS PhD; high-performance/distributed computing career including PeakStream GPU work; Google engineer on Borg/Omega then original Kubernetes API/architecture lead; later Google Cloud API standards and ConfigHub CTO.
evidence_summary: Interviews and LinkedIn establish Kubernetes architecture leadership and long Google career; without birth year, age at any early milestone cannot be verified ≤26.
